personality: Ancient, hungry, and then tamed. Its loyalty is grudging but complete.

cards.title: The Thing in the Lake
cards.text: No one in Silene knew where it came from. One day there was simply a dragon in the great lake outside the walls, as wide as a sea. When it came near the city its breath poisoned the air, and people died without being touched. The citizens armed themselves and marched out against it. They were beaten back, and after that they did not go out again.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900

cards.title: The Tribute
cards.text: To keep it from the walls, the city fed it two sheep every day. When the sheep grew few, they gave it one sheep and one person. When the sheep ran out, they drew lots among the children, and no family, rich or poor, was spared. For years the dragon lay in its lake and waited to be fed, until the day the lot fell on the king's own daughter.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900

cards.title: Led on a Girdle
cards.text: A stranger's spear brought it down at the lakeside. Wounded and tied with the princess's girdle, the dragon followed her into Silene as meekly as a dog, while the people who had fed it fled in terror. In the city square the knight killed it. It was so huge that it took four teams of oxen to drag its body out beyond the walls.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900
